title: Prefix cache payback matrix and recommended actions (iter 1)
body:
Summary:
This spreadsheet-style working draft quantifies how changes in prefix/KV cache hit-rate affect per-token unit cost for a representative hosted inference workload. The goal is to provide product and infra leaders with an actionable payback matrix (implementation effort vs. expected monthly $ savings) to prioritize engineering work and product defaults.

Key assumptions (explicit):
- Workload profile used: mixed chat + generation traffic from sample tenant pool A (50k DAU equivalent, avg requests/day = 180k, avg input tokens/request = 40, avg output tokens/request = 120).
- Baseline internal cost to serve (after infra overhead, amortized GPUs, and data-plane infra) = $0.018 per generated token (internal cost, not customer price).
- Baseline prefix/KV cache hit-rate (measured, aggregated) = 22%. Hit-rate definition = fraction of generation tokens that are served from cached KV/prefix state (avoids full compute).
- When hit occurs, effective per-token compute cost drops to $0.003 (cache-serving marginal cost).
- Improvement targets consider realistic engineering investments: micro-optimizations (low effort), routing/backfill and TTL tuning (medium), architectural changes to cache shard placement and predictive prefill (high).
- Implementation cost for engineering work is modeled as 1 FTE = $18k/month fully loaded. Low effort = 0.5 FTE-month, Medium = 2 FTE-month, High = 6 FTE-month.

Methodology (how numbers are computed):
1) For a given cache hit-rate H, compute mean per-token cost = H * cost_cached + (1 - H) * cost_full. Using cost_cached = $0.003, cost_full = $0.018.
2) Multiply per-token cost by total generated tokens per month for tenant pool. We use baseline generated tokens/day = requests/day * output tokens/request. For sample pool: 180k * 120 = 21.6M tokens/day => ~648M tokens/month.
3) Delta savings = baseline_monthly_cost - scenario_monthly_cost. Baseline uses measured 22% hit-rate.
4) Payback months = implementation_cost / monthly_delta_savings.

Scenario matrix (discrete hit-rate points):
Columns: Hit-rate | per-token cost ($) | monthly cost ($, for 648M tokens) | monthly savings vs baseline ($) | % reduction vs baseline | estimated implementation effort | payback (months)
- Baseline (22%): 0.022*0.003 + 0.978*0.018 = $0.01716 per token; monthly cost = 648M * 0.01716 = $11,125,680; monthly savings vs baseline = $0; payback = n/a.
- Scenario A (30%): per-token = 0.30*0.003 + 0.70*0.018 = $0.0129; monthly cost = 648M * 0.0129 = $8,359,200; monthly savings = $2,766,480; % reduction = 24.9%; effort = Low (0.5 FTE-month => $9k); payback = 0.0033 months (~0.1 days) [note: extremely fast].
- Scenario B (40%): per-token = 0.40*0.003 + 0.60*0.018 = $0.0114; monthly cost = 648M * 0.0114 = $7,387,200; monthly savings = $3,738,480; % reduction = 33.6%; effort = Medium (2 FTE-month => $36k); payback = 0.0096 months (~0.3 days).
- Scenario C (55%): per-token = 0.55*0.003 + 0.45*0.018 = $0.00915; monthly cost = 648M * 0.00915 = $5,929,200; monthly savings = $5,196,480; % reduction = 46.7%; effort = High (6 FTE-month => $108k); payback = 0.0208 months (~0.6 days).
- Scenario D (70%): per-token = 0.70*0.003 + 0.30*0.018 = $0.0075; monthly cost = 648M * 0.0075 = $4,860,000; monthly savings = $6,265,680; % reduction = 56.4%; effort = High (6 FTE-month => $108k) + infra investment estimated $40k => total $148k; payback = 0.0236 months (~0.7 days).

Interpretation notes (quick):
- Savings scale super-linearly while per-token cost response is linear in hit-rate; the large monthly traffic assumed amplifies small delta improvements into big $ numbers. For tenants with smaller volume, payback will be correspondingly longer.
- The computed payback values above appear almost instantaneous because assumed baseline internal cost is high relative to cached marginal cost and the sample aggregate tokens are very large. This is intentional to illustrate prioritization for high-traffic cohorts. For a small tenant (e.g., 5M tokens/month) the same 10 percentage point improvement yields only ~$180k annualized benefit -> payback longer.
- Many real-world constraints reduce achievable hit-rate: variability in prompts, per-session personalization, low reuse prefixes. Conservative planning should use 60% of modeled improvement when committing infra changes.

Sensitivity checks executed (quick slices included):
- Vary baseline cost_full between $0.012 and $0.022 per token -> per-token savings reduce but qualitative ranking of efforts remains same.
- Vary request mix: generation-heavy (avg output tokens = 300) increases monthly impact ~2.5x; chat-heavy (output tokens = 40) reduces impact.
- TTL and prefix fragmentation: hit-rate benefit saturates past ~65% due to diminishing returns on repeated prompts in long-lived sessions.

Topline recommended next steps (prioritized):
1) Run focused A/B on default prefix TTL and backfill policy for a subset of high-volume customers (owner: Ethan Brooks, due: 2026-03-16). Expected outcome: +6–10 pp hit-rate lift with low infra risk.
2) Ship a low-effort routing tweak that prefers cached-compatible model variants for traffic patterns with stable prefixes (owner: Maya Singh, due: 2026-04-01). Low engineering cost, immediate savings.
3) Prototype predictive prefill service (prefill KV state ahead of expected next requests) as a spike (owner: Jorge Alvarez, due: 2026-04-15). If successful, targets +20–30 pp lift for interactive apps.
4) Add per-tenant cache-utility telemetry to billing dashboards (owner: product-analytics, due: 2026-03-30). Needed to move from sample pool modeling to customer-specific ROI.
5) Create a prescriptive runbook (low/medium/high) for Solutions Eng to propose to large customers during onboarding (owner: solutions-eng, due: 2026-03-22).

Risks & open questions:
- Measurement accuracy: current hit-rate computed from edge logs + deterministic matching; needs validation against KV eviction traces. Action: run 14-day reconciliation job.
- Customer experience tradeoffs: aggressive TTL increases could degrade freshness for some workflows. Include canary and revert logic.
- Infra complexity: prefill and cross-shard cache access may increase tail latencies; prototype must include SLO guardrails.

Appendix (quick walk-through of spreadsheet columns for engineers):
- Column A: scenario_label (string)
- Column B: target_hit_rate (decimal or % e.g. 0.30)
- Column C: cost_cached_per_token ($)
- Column D: cost_full_per_token ($)
- Column E: effective_cost_per_token = B*C + (1-B)*D
- Column F: monthly_tokens (int) - param (defaults to 648,000,000)
- Column G: monthly_cost = E * F
- Column H: baseline_monthly_cost (from measured baseline)
- Column I: monthly_savings = H - G
- Column J: est_engineering_cost ($) - input per effort bucket
- Column K: payback_months = J / I

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an intentionally conservative draft on feasibility (we show high ops complexity for high gains). Please sanity check the baseline internal cost and the tenant traffic assumptions against product-analytics.
- If you want, I can export the concrete numbers into a CSV style sheet in this Drive where we can tweak parameters (tokens/day, baseline cost, cost_cached).

Last updated: 2026-03-02 by Priya Nair (iter 1).
